questions.questionText: What was the main characteristic of the American economy in the 1920s?
questions.explanation: The 1920s saw massive industrial growth, stock market speculation, and rising consumer culture.

questions.questionText: What event triggered the Great Depression?
questions.explanation: The October 1929 stock market crash wiped out investments and triggered widespread economic collapse.

questions.questionText: Who was the US President during the early Great Depression?
questions.explanation: Hoover served as president when the Depression began but was blamed for inadequate response.

questions.questionText: What was the New Deal?
questions.explanation: The New Deal was FDR's comprehensive program of relief, recovery, and reform to address the Depression.

questions.questionText: What was Prohibition in the USA?

options.text: Ban on alcohol production and sale

questions.explanation: Prohibition (1920-1933) banned alcohol, leading to speakeasies and organized crime growth.

questions.questionText: Who were the 'Robber Barons'?

options.text: Wealthy industrialists accused of unethical business practices

questions.explanation: Robber Barons were industrialists like Rockefeller and Carnegie who built monopolies through ruthless tactics.

questions.questionText: What was the Dust Bowl?

options.text: Severe drought and dust storms in the Great Plains

questions.explanation: The Dust Bowl (1930s) destroyed farms and displaced millions of farmers in the Great Plains.

questions.questionText: What were the main features of the New Deal?

options.text: Relief programs, financial reform, and industrial recovery

questions.explanation: The New Deal included relief for unemployed, recovery for economy, and reforms to prevent future crises.

questions.questionText: What was the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)?

options.text: Federal program for regional development and electrification

questions.explanation: TVA brought electricity, flood control, and economic development to one of America's poorest regions.

questions.questionText: How did mass production change American industry?

options.text: Made goods affordable through assembly line techniques

questions.explanation: Assembly line production reduced costs and made consumer goods like automobiles accessible to millions.

questions.questionText: What role did installment buying play in the 1920s economy?

options.text: Fueled consumer spending and contributed to debt bubble

questions.explanation: Installment plans allowed Americans to buy consumer goods on credit, creating artificial demand.

questions.questionText: What was the Social Security Act of 1935?
questions.explanation: Social Security established retirement pensions and unemployment insurance, creating America's safety net.

questions.questionText: How did the Great Depression affect American workers?

options.text: Mass unemployment, poverty, and labor unrest

questions.explanation: Unemployment peaked at 25%, banks failed, farms were foreclosed, and families lost everything.

questions.questionText: What was the Works Progress Administration (WPA)?

options.text: Federal jobs program employing millions on public works

questions.explanation: WPA employed 8 million workers on construction projects, theaters, and arts during the Depression.

questions.questionText: Analyze the causes of the Great Depression.

options.text: Overproduction, speculation, banking failures, and global factors
Single cause like stock market crash

questions.explanation: The Depression resulted from overproduction, unequal wealth distribution, stock speculation, bank failures, and Smoot-Hawley tariffs.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the effectiveness of the New Deal in resolving the Depression.

options.text: Provided relief but full recovery came with WWII

questions.explanation: New Deal relief programs helped millions survive, but full economic recovery required wartime mobilization.

questions.questionText: To what extent did the New Deal transform American government?

options.text: Established permanent federal role in economy and social welfare

questions.explanation: New Deal created regulatory agencies, social programs, and expanded federal government responsibility for welfare.

questions.questionText: Analyze the impact of capitalism on American society during this period.

options.text: Created wealth divide with boom for some and poverty for others

questions.explanation: Capitalist growth created a wealthy elite while many workers faced poverty, with disproportionate impact on minorities.

questions.questionText: How did the Great Depression affect racial minorities in America?

options.text: Disproportionate poverty and discrimination in New Deal programs
Had no special impact on minorities

questions.explanation: Black Americans faced 'last hired, first fired' discrimination and exclusion from many New Deal benefits.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of 1920s prosperity and Depression-era reforms.

options.text: Shaped modern consumer economy and regulatory state

questions.explanation: The era established patterns of consumer credit, labor rights, financial regulation, and social security that persist today.
